archetype.name: Pocket Passer (high-volume)
archetype.definition: An eleventh-year rhythm thrower who wins from a clean pocket with quick, on-time decisions, sack avoidance and a deep receiver room, and who is asked to throw a lot because his defense keeps games high-scoring.

report.headline: Volume and protection keep Dak productive while his accuracy quietly slips
report.take:
Prescott is a high-volume pocket passer on a team that has to score every week. Dallas's defense ranks 32nd of 32 in EPA allowed, so he is throwing 37.8 times a game, which drives his 5th-ranked yardage and a 4,348-yard pace. The efficiency underneath that volume is good rather than special. His 0.167 EPA per dropback ranks 15th, well clear of the 0.034 league average, but his yards per attempt (6.77, 25th) and CPOE (0.97, 22nd) sit in the middle of the pack.

Two things carry his season. The first is the pocket. He takes a sack on only 3.5% of dropbacks, 3rd in the league against a 6.9% average, and only 10.9% of his pressures turn into sacks, best among 38 charted passers. He gets the ball out in 2.77 seconds behind a line that allows the 4th-lowest hit rate. The second is his receivers. CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy all produce more than 0.3 EPA per target, and the throws that get past 10 air yards return 0.371 EPA a play. On only 25 deep attempts he has a CPOE of 8.2. When he throws at or beyond the sticks, the offense works.

The season totals hide a real slide in ball placement. His bad-throw rate has climbed to 14.2% from 11.2% last year, and over his last five games his CPOE is -2.8 with EPA per dropback down to 0.066. Part of that is the schedule. Weeks 5 and 6 were back-to-back losses to Tampa (2nd-ranked defense) and Green Bay (7th), with his two negative-EPA games of the year. But a flat Week 8 against Arizona's 27th-ranked defense, with four sacks, says it is not only the opponents. The pressure-to-sack rate is also far better than anything in his career (24.4% last year, 34.8% in 2023), so some sacks will come back. Four of his five interceptions have come on intermediate throws, three of them over the middle.

Career context keeps this from being alarming. His 2018 through 2022 seasons had bad-throw rates of 14.4% to 17%, so this year is a return toward his norm rather than a collapse. He rebounded from a poor 2024 to 0.191 EPA per play last season. Expect the volume to hold, the sack luck to fade a little, and the efficiency to settle between his slump and his strong first month, with softer defenses doing some of the lifting.

strengths.title: Sack avoidance behind a sturdy line
strengths.body: He turns pressure into sacks less often than any qualifier, and his line keeps him from being hit at one of the lowest rates in the league. The cause is partly him, with quick reads and a 2.77-second release, and partly the protection. The rate is well below anything in his career, so expect some regression, but the low sack total is a real skill and not only luck.

strengths.title: Efficient at and past the sticks
strengths.body: Throws of 10-plus air yards return far more EPA than his underneath game, and his deep ball has been placed well above expectation. That reflects having three productive wideouts who win outside, especially Pickens. The deep sample is only 25 attempts, so the exact rate will cool, but the downfield profile fits the personnel.

strengths.title: Defense-driven volume floor
strengths.body: With the league's worst defense behind him, Dallas rarely gets to sit on a lead, so he keeps throwing. That keeps his yardage near the top of the league even on inefficient days. The setup is structural and should last as long as the defense stays this porous.

concerns.title: Ball placement has slipped
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate is up 3 points from last year, and his completion percentage over expected has gone negative over the past five games. Some of that came against two top-seven defenses, but the Arizona game shows it is not purely the opponents. His career suggests this is a return toward his long-run norm rather than decline, which caps his upside more than it threatens his floor.

concerns.title: Middle-of-field interceptions
concerns.body: Most of his interceptions have come on intermediate throws, and the middle of the field is by far his least productive area despite five touchdowns there. That is the window where his recent misplacement does the most damage. Interceptions have long been a weak spot in his career rankings, so his decent 1.7% rate this year is more likely to rise than fall.

concerns.title: Dead weight in the quick game
concerns.body: Throws behind the line of scrimmage have cost Dallas real points, despite a high completion rate. The tight end, a natural safety valve, has produced negative EPA per target. This looks like a scheme and personnel issue rather than a Prescott flaw, and it drags down an otherwise efficient short game.

trend.note: He opened with three strong EPA games, then posted negative games against Tampa Bay and Green Bay, bounced back with a sharp game in Philadelphia and went flat against Arizona. The swings follow opponent quality, but the accuracy has drifted down underneath them.

nextGame.headline: Depleted Colts secondary is the right spot for a reset
nextGame.body:
Indianapolis ranks 20th against the pass and 25th in EPA allowed on short throws, which is exactly where Prescott's high-percentage game lives. The Colts allow an average 18 PPR points a game to quarterbacks and sit near the bottom in hit rate, so his clean pocket should hold. The resistance is at the top of the depth chart. The Colts have held WR1s and especially WR2s below their norms, which points volume and efficiency toward Flournoy in the third-receiver role the Colts have leaked to. Dallas is favored by 6 with a 51.5 total.

Availability tilts his way. Cornerback Justin Walley, a 72%-snap starter, is out, and Cam Taylor-Britt is on injured reserve, which thins a secondary already struggling against third options. On his side, Jake Ferguson is questionable with an ankle sprain and Luke Schoonmaker is out, leaving thin tight end depth against a defense that has given tight ends extra production. Ferguson has been inefficient this year, though, so his absence would mostly shift short targets to the wideouts rather than cost much. The game is under a retractable roof.

keyMatchups.title: Flournoy against a thinned secondary
keyMatchups.body: The Colts have been among the league's worst at limiting third receivers, and they are now missing a starting corner. Flournoy has been efficient in that role, so this is the likeliest place for Prescott's volume to turn into chunk gains. The outside starters, by contrast, face a defense that has held top two receivers down.

keyMatchups.title: Short game against soft underneath
keyMatchups.body: His 0-9 yard throws are his most reliable play at a 72.6% completion rate, and Indianapolis is bottom-eight against short passes. That should let him rebuild rhythm and a better completion rate over expected without forcing the intermediate middle throws that have produced his interceptions.

keyMatchups.title: Colts run game controls volume
keyMatchups.body: Indianapolis's passing offense is one of the league's worst, but it runs efficiently and leans on the run, against a Dallas run defense ranked 29th. If the Colts grind the clock, Prescott gets fewer possessions than usual and a likely lead may cut his late volume. That risk is to his yardage, not his efficiency.

nextGame.watch: Whether his ball placement rebounds against a short-handed secondary. A positive CPOE game here would mark the recent slump as opponent-driven, while another poorly placed game against a soft defense would make it a trend.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is the most bankable part of his profile. A last-ranked defense keeps Dallas throwing, so expect around 245-280 passing yards a game, with 1.5-2.0 touchdowns and 0.5-0.8 interceptions. The protection is real, but a pressure-to-sack rate this far below his career will drift upward, so expect a few more sacks than his first eight games. His efficiency should land between the hot start and the recent slump, near his season level and above the league, helped by strong receivers and a red-zone touchdown rate that has held despite a low completion rate there.

The question is accuracy. His career shows bad-throw rates in this range in several solid seasons, so this looks like a normal version of him rather than a falling one. If the rate keeps climbing, though, the intermediate interceptions will grow with it. Rushing stays a small bonus, roughly 8-16 yards a game, with the occasional short touchdown.
swingFactors: Whether his CPOE and bad-throw rate recover to 2025 levels
Dallas's defense forcing shootouts versus allowing clock-control games
How far his sack avoidance regresses

confidence.note: Eight games with a stable role and a long career track record, but the accuracy dip and the outlier sack-avoidance rate are still settling.
